title: Valafind: Find files by what they mean
shortDescription: Find files by what they mean, not what they're called. Describe a document, photo, recording or video in your own words, in any of 100+ languages, and Valafind finds it. Everything runs on your computer: no cloud, no account, no telemetry.
description:
Find files by what they mean, not what they're called.

Press Ctrl+Alt+Space, describe what you're looking for in your own words, and Valafind finds the file, even when it's written in another language and named scan_0042.pdf.

It works for documents, photos, audio and video:
• "where did we negotiate the deposit?" finds the e-mail and the lease
• "a red car in the snow" finds the picture
• "the meeting about the budget" finds the recording

Valafind reads your documents, PDFs, slides, spreadsheets, e-mail and code, looks at your photos, and listens to your recordings and videos. It understands them in more than 100 languages, so you can ask the way you'd ask a colleague. The highlighted passage in each result shows why it matched.

Nothing leaves your computer
The AI model (EmbeddingGemma 2 by Google DeepMind) runs locally and is built into the app: no cloud, no account, no telemetry. Your files, your index and your searches stay on your computer, and the index is readable only by you.

Your everyday files first
Valafind starts with the files you actually use, your recent and frequent documents, and then works through the rest. Documents come first, then pictures, audio and video. New, changed, moved and deleted files are picked up within seconds.

Stays out of your way
Indexing uses only the CPU and disk your computer isn't using. Valafind measures the load every two seconds and slows down when you're compiling, gaming or on a call, then speeds up again when the machine is quiet. You choose the limits for CPU, disk and GPU use, which folders to index, and whether to pause on battery. When everything is indexed, it just shows a quiet ✓.

Valafind is open source (github.com/ffMathy/valafind). Buying it here supports its development.
